`POST /v1/contracts/customerBalances/list` is the bearer-secured detailed balance read. Its payload schema requires `customer_id`, although the request-body wrapper is not marked required; omitted-body and top-level unknown-field behavior remain undocumented. Optional access-window filters, balance and ledger expansions, contract and archive inclusion, feature-gated zero exclusion, and JSON-body cursor pagination are available. HTTP 200 is an object requiring `data` and nullable `next_page`; `data` is the Commit-or-Credit union. The endpoint's body `limit` is 1-25 and defaults to 25, unlike the separate pagination authority's query-parameter convention and general 100 cap.

`include_archived` says exactly "archived credits and credits from archived contracts." Commit alone exposes `archived_at`; Credit has no corresponding property. This is not enough to determine archived-commit inclusion or archived-credit status despite the contract-archive authority saying associated commits and credits are archived.

The calculated balance excludes expired and upcoming segments, includes future-dated manual entries on active segments, and ordinarily matches ledger sum. If negative manual entries exceed positive remaining value, however, it is floored at zero.

> [!warning] Contradiction
> This non-negative floor qualifies the existing broad signed-ledger-sum statement. The OpenAPI page also serializes uppercase, often expanded tokens such as `PREPAID_COMMIT_EXPIRATION`, `POSTPAID_COMMIT_INITIAL_BALANCE`, and `CREDIT_EXPIRATION`, while the remaining-balance guide uses lowercase and sometimes differently named `prepaid_commit_expiration`, `postpaid_initial_balance`, and `credit_segment_expiration`. Do not infer normalization or one-to-one equivalence; preserve each surface's exact names.
warnings: Calculated balance can be zero while signed ledger sum is negative after excessive negative manual entries.
Ledger enum differences include more than casing, especially CREDIT_EXPIRATION versus credit_segment_expiration.
Archive wording and response fields do not establish archived-commit inclusion or archived-credit status.

The detailed view is bearer-secured `POST /v1/contracts/customerBalances/list`. Its JSON payload requires the customer UUID and can filter by access-window dates, with exclusive `effective_before`; the body wrapper itself is not marked required. HTTP 200 requires an object containing a Commit-or-Credit `data` array and nullable `next_page`. This endpoint puts `next_page` and a 1-25, default-25 `limit` in the JSON body, unlike the general pagination authority's query parameters and 100 cap.

`include_contract_balances` requests contract-level records. `include_archived` says "archived credits and credits from archived contracts," while Commit alone exposes `archived_at` and Credit does not. The contract-archive authority separately says associated commits and credits are archived. These surfaces do not establish omitted-flag defaults, archived-commit inclusion, archived-credit status, hierarchy effects, response ordering, cursor lifetime, or snapshot consistency.
warnings: Preserve the exact repeated-credit archive wording and the Commit-only archived_at field.
Endpoint body pagination differs from the API-wide query-parameter convention.

The `listBalances` response models access- and invoice-schedule `amount`, `unit_price`, and `quantity` as numbers. Both schedule schemas make `credit_type` optional; on this page the referenced type requires only UUID `id` and string `name` and does not expose `is_currency`. The example uses `USD (cents)`, but this endpoint independently defines no USD, non-USD, or custom-unit denomination, precision, conversion, or rounding rule. Apply the dedicated currency and custom-unit authorities rather than inferring a universal scale from this response example.
warnings: credit_type is optional in both schedule schemas and this endpoint does not expose is_currency.
The USD (cents) example cannot establish non-USD or custom-unit encoding.

The `listBalances` Commit and Credit response schemas can each expose optional `custom_fields` through an arbitrary-key object whose additional-property values are strings. The Commit field is annotated as entity `commit`; the Credit field is annotated `contract_credit`. This endpoint does not define key format, value length, field count, visibility, redaction, permissions, availability, or unset-value behavior.
warnings: The contract_credit annotation is surface-specific and should not be renamed to credit without authority.
No endpoint-level key, count, visibility, redaction, or availability limits are documented.
